{"body":"# ask-dora skill family

Date: 2026-08-31
Status: ready-for-agent
Source: grill in this repo, 2026-08-31. Glossary: `CONTEXT.md` (ask-dora section).
Related: [Local use-case runner](../local-use-cases/spec.md) and issues #79–#83. This spec does not redo the harness CLI.

## Problem Statement

An internal Scalekit teammate opens a coding agent and wants help with Dora.

Today the shipped skill talks only to the Runner. It says: run `dora review --quick`, then fix, until exit 0. That is one job.

The teammate’s real start is a sentence: they type a command and describe an agent they want to run on this machine. Or they ask a normal Dora question (review, fix, unused). There is no one skill that routes both.

The harness already has a grill skill (`grill-routine`) and a routine folder. That grill is not the front door. It does not ask “is this loop-able?” first. It does not check Scalekit connectors. It does not copy skills into the routine. It is not written as a small family.

Matt-style idea-to-ship maps do not fit. This product is not “any software idea → ship code.” It is a **routine idea** → a **local** agent that can **loop**.

## Solution

Ship four skills under one add: `npx skills add saif-shines/doraval`.

1. **`ask-dora`** — the only name the human must remember. User-typed router. They type `/ask-dora` plus any Dora question or a routine idea.
2. **`review-with-dora`** — the old Runner loop (review → fix → exit 0). Replaces the skill named `doraval`.
3. **`grilling-for-routine`** — interview for a routine idea. Replaces `grill-routine`.
4. **`writing-for-routine`** — how to write the unattended night prompt. Original text. Same craft as a good agent document (steps, done-when, no second-person). Do not cite or copy another pack.

`discover-connectors` already exists in Scalekit. Point at it. Do not author a second skill with that name.

**Route**

- A Dora job (review, fix, unused, scan) → `review-with-dora` or the 
matching `dora` verb.
- A **routine idea** (loop, recurring, or an agent that should keep running locally) → the routine flow.

**Routine flow**

1. Is it **loop-able**? Can the same prompt run on an interval? If no: say why. Stop. Do not write a routine. Route if it is a normal Dora job.
2. `grilling-for-routine`.
3. Practicality check: live Scalekit connector catalog via `discover-connectors`. Say what exists. Say what an interval job cannot do.
4. `writing-for-routine` writes the night prompt.
5. **Routine copy**: duplicate skill folders into the routine. Source is a name on this machine, a local path, or a GitHub URL. Never edit the original.
6. One live run (print the command, or run it). Missing Hermes: print official install steps. Do not fake a pass.
7. If that run works → **loop** on Hermes. Default interval 1 hour. Dora stays off OAuth. Token fail → `hermes mcp login`.

`dora harness new` starts `ask-dora`, which loads `grilling-for-routine` when the ask is a routine idea.

## User Stories

1. As an internal teammate, I want to type `/ask-dora` plus any Dora question, so that I do not have to remember four skill names.
2. As a teammate, I want `/ask-dora` to work when I am not talking about a routine, so that I can still review, fix, or scan.
3. As a teammate, I want `/ask-dora always poll the ooo-holidays channel and create Google Calendar events` to start the routine flow, so that a routine idea has one start.
4. As a teammate, I want the first check to be “is this loop-able?”, so that a webhook or a one-off chat job is not saved as a routine.
5. As a teammate, I want a clear why when an idea is not loop-able, so that I know what to change or which Dora job to run instead.
6. As a teammate, I want no routine folder when the idea is not loop-able, so that disk does not hold a job that cannot loop.
7. As a teammate, I want the grill to ask until the night prompt is specific, so that an unattended pass has enough information.
8. As a
 teammate, I want the grill to collect skills to run, skills to refer to, and the Scalekit Agent Gateway MCP URL, so that the night pass has a gate.
9. As a teammate, I want a default shared MCP URL reused unless I override it, so that I do not paste it every time.
10. As a teammate, I want the agent to look up Scalekit connectors, so that I hear what is possible before the night prompt is written.
11. As a teammate, I want to hear when a needed connector is missing, so that I do not schedule a job that cannot call the tool.
12. As a teammate, I want to hear when an interval job cannot do the idea (push, webhook, human in the loop every tick), so that I do not confuse a loop with a chat app.
13. As a teammate, I want the night prompt written for an agent, so that the loop does not read like a human chat.
14. As a teammate, I want that prompt to use steps and a done-when, so that the night agent can tell finished from not finished.
15. As a teammate, I want no second-person identity in the night prompt, so that the unattended agent is not told “you are.”
16. As a teammate, I want to name a skill, or give a local path, or give a GitHub URL, so that I can bring skills I already have.
17. As a teammate, I want Dora to look up a named skill on this machine first (project `skills/`, then home), so that a short name is enough when the skill is already here.
18. As a teammate, I want Dora to ask for a path or a GitHub URL when the name is missing, so that it does not invent a registry.
19. As a teammate, I want those skills copied into the routine, so that later edits do not change the original.
20. As a teammate, I want routine-level edits on the copy only, so that I can tune one job without breaking other jobs.
21. As a teammate, I want one live run before Hermes, so that a bad prompt does not fire every hour.
22. As a teammate, I want the one-pass command printed, so that I can run it in another terminal.
23. As a teammate, I want an offer to run that pass
 if Hermes is present, so that I do not have to copy the command.
24. As a teammate without Hermes, I want official install steps and no fake pass, so that I am not told it worked.
25. As a teammate, I want the loop to start only after that run works, so that Hermes does not get a failing job.
26. As a teammate, I want the default interval to stay 1 hour, so that I am not forced to pick a schedule first.
27. As a teammate, I want to set the interval after the good run, so that I configure the loop at the moment it becomes real.
28. As a teammate, I want `dora harness boot / pause / resume / list / open` after a routine exists, so that the life of the job has verbs.
29. As a teammate, I want Dora off the OAuth / magic-link path, so that a night tick does not wait on a browser.
30. As a teammate, I want a dead token to stop and tell me `hermes mcp login`, so that a refresh fail is not a silent success.
31. As a teammate, I want a dead Scalekit connected account to stop and tell me to open the provider link again, so that I can fix the provider side.
32. As a maintainer, I want `ask-dora` to be user-invoked, so that it does not spend description tokens on every turn unless the human types it.
33. As a maintainer, I want `review-with-dora`, `grilling-for-routine`, and `writing-for-routine` to be reachable by `ask-dora`, so that the router can name a real next skill.
34. As a maintainer, I want the skill named `doraval` gone, so that there are not two front doors.
35. As a maintainer, I want `grill-routine` renamed to `grilling-for-routine`, so that there is one interview skill.
36. As a maintainer, I want `dora harness new` to start `ask-dora`, so that the CLI and the slash command share one door.
37. As a maintainer, I want `npx skills add saif-shines/doraval` to install all four skills, so that one add is enough.
38. As a maintainer, I want each of the four to pass `dora review --quick`, so that a draft does not ship.
39. As a maintainer, I want origin
al skill text, so that we do not cite or copy another pack in shipped files.
40. As a maintainer, I want MIT on this repo to stay as it is, so that license is not a new debate.
41. As a maintainer, I want README, website, and the family to name the same four skills, so that docs lockstep holds.
42. As a maintainer, I want help text that still talks to the Runner for `dora` verbs, so that Reader and Runner stay split on CLI help.
43. As a first reader, I want wording for an internal teammate, so that this is not sold as a customer product yet.
44. As a later reader, I want objects that are not locked to Scalekit customers only, so that opening up later does not rewrite the folder.
45. As a teammate, I want one machine and one user, so that I do not need a fleet.
46. As a teammate, I want no first sample routine idea forced by this spec, so that the grill stays generic.
47. As a teammate, I want Slack, Discord, Google Calendar, and Webflow to stay connectors on the idea, so that the harness does not assume one app.
48. As a teammate, I want empty `/ask-dora` to print the map, so that I can see Dora jobs and the routine flow.
49. As a teammate, I want the map to say when the routine flow applies (routine, loop, recurring, routine idea), so that I do not think every ask becomes a cron job.
50. As a coding agent running `ask-dora`, I want facts (catalog, Hermes present, skill on disk) looked up, so that I do not ask the human for what I can see.
51. As a coding agent, I want decisions left to the human, so that I do not invent a slug, a connector, or a loop interval.
52. As a coding agent writing the night prompt, I want `writing-for-routine` as the single home for that craft, so that the rules are not repeated in `ask-dora`.
53. As a coding agent grilling, I want `grilling-for-routine` as the single home for the interview, so that the router stays a map.
54. As a maintainer, I want this spec to reuse the harness CLI, so that we do not rebuild boot, pause,
 or the routine folder writer.
55. As a maintainer, I want kit `CONTEXT.md` left alone, so that loop words stay in doraval.
56. As a teammate, I want optional `dora review` on copied skill directories, so that I can check them if I want and skip if I do not.

## Implementation Decisions

- This spec owns the **skill family**. The harness CLI and routine folder contract stay with the local use-case runner spec. Do not re-open those verbs except where a name must change (`grill-routine` → `grilling-for-routine`; start `ask-dora` from `dora harness new`).
- Product words: **routine idea** (typed sentence), **routine** (saved folder), **loop-able** (early check), **loop** (Hermes cron after one good run), **routine copy** (duplicate into the routine).
- Four shipped skills. No skill named `doraval`. No skill named `grill-routine`.
- `ask-dora` is a router only. It does not contain the review loop, the interview, or the night-prompt craft.
- `review-with-dora` holds the current Runner loop. Move that behavior. Then delete the old skill name.
- `grilling-for-routine` and `writing-for-routine` are original. Write them for a local agent that can loop. Do not cite another author or pack in the shipped files. Do not vendor another pack’s text.
- Craft that `writing-for-routine` must teach: steps, completion criteria, no second-person identity, no em dashes, one home per rule, progressive disclosure of reference. Apply that craft to the night prompt, and to the skill files themselves.
- `discover-connectors` is a pointer target only. Do not copy the Scalekit catalog into this repo. Do not ship a second skill with that name.
- Name lookup: project skills, then home skills, then ask for a path or GitHub URL. No public registry in this pass.
- Routine copy is a duplicate. Night-pass edits land on the copy. The original is not a write target.
- Loop-able is a shape check (interval job vs webhook / one-off / always-human). Connector presence is the next check. Both 
run before the night prompt is written.
- One live run before Hermes. Same missing-Hermes behavior as the harness spec.
- Default interval 1 hour. Ask for the interval after a good run, not during the first grill.
- Dora does not sit on OAuth. Token and connected-account failures stay as in the harness spec.
- First wording: internal teammate. No forced sample idea.
- Docs lockstep when the family ships: website content, README, the four skills, and help lines that would otherwise disagree.
- Seams agreed 2026-08-31: (1) `dora review --quick` on each of the four skill directories, (2) docs lockstep test extended to the four names, (3) `dora harness new` names `ask-dora` / `grilling-for-routine` and does not name `grill-routine` or the old `doraval` skill.

## Testing Decisions

A good test checks what a teammate can read on disk or in CLI output. It does not run the interview. It does not call Scalekit. It does not start Hermes.

### Seams (agreed)

1. **Skill folders.** `dora review --quick` on each of the four directories. Exit 0. Assert the router names the other three. Assert the grill names the gate and loop-able-first. Assert the writer names steps and done-when. Do not automate the chat.
2. **Docs lockstep.** README, website, and the family name the same four skills and the same `dora harness` verbs. Extend the existing harness docs test.
3. **CLI pointer.** `dora harness new` starts `ask-dora` / `grilling-for-routine`. It does not name `grill-routine` or the old `doraval` skill.

### Modules under test

- The four skill directories (review plus named contracts above).
- Docs lockstep test.
- Harness `new` help / start text.

### Prior art

- Existing grill-skill review test.
- Existing `harness-docs` lockstep test.
- Closed command tree tests for harness verbs (do not duplicate here).

## Out of Scope

- Rebuilding `dora harness` boot, pause, resume, list, open, or the routine folder writer.
- A new CLI beside Dora.
- Copyin
g or citing another skill pack in shipped files.
- An idea-to-ship software map (spec, tickets, implement as the product flow).
- A public skill registry.
- A second `discover-connectors` skill in this repo.
- Dora on the OAuth / magic-link path.
- Dora installing Hermes.
- Live Scalekit or Hermes in CI.
- Company setup on more than one machine.
- Customer-facing wording.
- A forced first sample idea.
- Writing loop terms into kit `CONTEXT.md`.
- Implementing in the spec session. Spec first. Tickets next.

## Further Notes

Glossary lives in doraval `CONTEXT.md` (ask-dora section). Grill closed 2026-08-31.

Harness runtime and OAuth stories stay in `.scratch/local-use-cases/spec.md` and #79–#83.

Next: `/to-tickets` in this thread or a fresh one. Then `/implement` per ticket in a fresh session.

  candidate.

  agent, any project. Project unused still never marks a Global Skill.

### Docs

- Website, README, skill, and style prompt use the new command names. Empty `dora` is `--help`.

### Docs

- Feature release requires docs lockstep (`AGENTS.md`): website, README, and
  the shipped skill must match the binary before tag.

80→### Features

1→---
name: pushify
version: 1.1.0
category: Development Workflow
license: MIT
description: "Run pre-push lefthook checks and iteratively fix failures (up to 3 iterations, then escalate). Invoke when: (a) about to push and wanting hooks to pass cleanly, (b) `git push` has just failed on a pre-push hook and the failure needs to be driven to resolution, or (c) preparing a clean working tree without pushing — e.g. before opening a Draft MR for early review."
metadata:
  author: pshutsin
  audience: developers
10→---

# Pushify

Run all pre-push lefthook hooks and fix failures iteratively until everything passes. All pre-push hooks must pass.

## Workflow

### Step 1: Run lefthook

20→```bash
mise exec -- lefthook run pre-push
```

If all pass → done, tell user "All pre-push checks pass. Ready to push."

### Step 2: Identify failures

Read the output and identify which hooks failed. Each failed hook has a fix strategy below.

name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - 'v*'
  # Re-run publish from main (new script) without a version bump.
  # create-release / homebrew stay tag-only so we do not open a second release.
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: write

env:
  FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24: true

jobs:
  build-binaries:
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          # macOS x64 (Intel) - bun cross-compiles the target regardless of host arch;
          # macos-13 (Intel) hosted runner pool is retired/unassignable, use macos-latest
          - runner: macos-latest
            target: bun-darwin-x64
            binary: doraval-darwin-x64

          # macOS arm64 (Apple Silicon)
          - runner: macos-latest
            target: bun-darwin-arm64
            binary: doraval-darwin-arm64

          # Linux x64 (glibc)
          - runner: ubuntu-latest
            target: bun-linux-x64
            binary: doraval-linux-x64

          # Linux arm64 (use arm runner so the arm64 native deps are installed)
          - runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            target: bun-linux-arm64
            binary: doraval-linux-arm64

          # Windows x64 (native host — no cross-compile dance needed)
          - runner: windows-latest
            target: bun-windows-x64
            binary: doraval-win32-x64.exe

    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
      - run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Build compiled binary
        shell: bash
        run: |
          bun build ./src/cli/index.ts --compile --target ${{ matrix.target }} --outfile ${{ matrix.binary }}

      - name: Upload binary
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: ${{ matrix.binary }}
          path: ${{ matrix.binary }}

  smoke-binaries:
    needs: build-binaries
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          # darwin-arm64 host is available; darwin-x64 has no free native runner
          # and ships without a pre-publish smoke run (covered by the
          # post-publish npx verification in publish-npm instead).
          - runner: macos-latest
            binary: doraval-darwin-arm64
          - runner: ubuntu-latest
            binary: doraval-linux-x64
          - runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm

1→---
name: grilling-for-routine
description: >-
  Use when ask-dora routes a routine idea, when running dora harness new,
  or when grilling a loop-able idea into a routine. Collect skills to run,
  skills to refer to, and the Scalekit Agent Gateway MCP URL.
---

# grilling-for-routine
10→
Use this grill with an internal teammate. Turn a routine idea into a routine.
Hermes is the agent. Do not pick a sample product.

## Loop-able

First check: can the same prompt run on an interval?

Loop-able: a poll, a scan, or a check that can repeat with no human on each tick.

20→Not loop-able: a webhook, a push listener, a one-off, or a job that needs a human every tick.

If not loop-able: say why. Do not write a routine folder. If it is a Dora job, load review-with-dora. Stop.

## Connectors

Load `discover-connectors` (Scalekit). Look up the live catalog. Say what exists. Say if a needed connector is missing. Do not vendor that catalog here.

An interval job cannot do a push, a webhook, or a human in the loop every tick. Say so when the idea needs one of those.

30→## Gate

Collect all three before you write the unattended prompt:

1. Skills to **run** (directories the night pass loads)
2. Skills to **refer to** (directories the prompt may cite)
3. Scalekit Agent Gateway **MCP URL**

A default shared MCP URL may already be saved. Reuse it. Ask before you override it for this routine.

40→## Routine copy

A skill source is a name, a local path, or a GitHub URL.

Name lookup: project `skills/`, then home skills, then ask for a path or a GitHub URL. Do not invent a registry.

Dora copies each skill folder into the routine. Night-pass edits land on the copy. Do not write the original.

Offer `dora review --quick` on each copy. The teammate can skip.

50→## Order

1. Run the loop-able check.
2. Ask what the routine idea does until the night prompt is specific.
3. Collect the gate. Offer a readable slug. The teammate picks or renames it.
4. Run the connector check.
5. Load `writing-for-routine`. Write the night prompt.
6. Print the one-pass command. If Hermes is present, offer to run it. If Hermes is missing, print official install steps. Do not fake a pass.
7. Write the routine folder only after that pass, or after the teammate accepts the printed command. Save copies the skills into the routine. Then offer `dora review --quick` on each copy. The teammate can skip.
8. After `dora harness boot`, tell the teammate to run `hermes mcp login scalekit`. Dora does not run that login. If a refresh token dies, run that command again. If the Scalekit connected account is dead, open the provider link again.
60→
Do not ask for the loop interval during this grill. Default is 1 hour. Ask after a good run.

```bash
dora harness new --accept --yes --slug <slug> --prompt-file <prompt.md> --mcp-url <url> --skills-run <name|path|url> --skills-refer <name|path|url>
```

MUST run the loop-able check first.
MUST collect the gate before save.
MUST copy named skills into the routine.
70→MUST NOT write the original skill directory.
MUST NOT invent a registry, a slug, a connector, or a loop interval.
MUST NOT write the folder when the idea is not loop-able.
MUST NOT write the folder before the one pass or an accepted printed command.

    client_secret=os.getenv("SCALEKIT_CLIENT_SECRET"),
    env_url=os.getenv("SCALEKIT_ENVIRONMENT_URL"),

90→        break

100→```

110→- tool name

- what it does

- optional fields from `input_schema.properties`

1→---
name: grilling-for-routine
description: >-
  Use when ask-dora routes a routine idea, when running dora harness new,
  or when grilling a loop-able idea into a routine. Collect skills to run,
  skills to refer to, and the Scalekit Agent Gateway MCP URL.
---

# grilling-for-routine
10→
Use this grill with an internal teammate. Turn a routine idea into a routine.
Hermes is the agent. Do not pick a sample product.

## Loop-able

First check: can the same prompt run on an interval?

Loop-able: a poll, a scan, or a check that can repeat with no human on each tick.

20→Not loop-able: a webhook, a push listener, a one-off, or a job that needs a human every tick.

If not loop-able: say why. Do not write a routine folder. If it is a Dora job, load review-with-dora. Stop.

## Connectors

Load `discover-connectors` (Scalekit). Look up the live catalog. Say what exists. Say if a needed connector is missing. Do not vendor that catalog here.

An interval job cannot do a push, a webhook, or a human in the loop every tick. Say so when the idea needs one of those.

30→## Gate

Collect all three before you write the unattended prompt:

1. Skills to **run** (optional extra SKILL.md folders the night pass loads).
   Say **none** if the MCP tools are enough.
2. Skills to **refer to** (optional folders the prompt may cite).
   Say **none** if none.
3. Scalekit Agent Gateway **MCP URL** (required).
   Slack, GitHub, and other connectors live here. A connector is not a skill.
40→
A default shared MCP URL may already be saved. Reuse it. Ask before you override it for this routine.

If no matching skill is on disk, do not invent one. Offer **none**, a local path, or a GitHub URL. Do not treat a missing Slack or GitHub skill as a blocker.

## Routine copy

A skill source is a name, a local path, or a GitHub URL.

Name lookup: project `skills/`, then home skills, then ask for a path or a GitHub URL. Do not invent a registry.
50→
Dora copies each skill folder into the routine. Night-pass edits land on the copy. Do not write the original.

Offer `dora review --quick` on each copy. The teammate can skip.

## Order

1. Run the loop-able check.
2. Ask what the routine idea does until the night prompt is specific.
3. Collect the gate. Offer a readable slug. The teammate picks or renames it.
60→4. Run the connector check.
5. Load `writing-for-routine`. Write the night prompt.
6. Print the one-pass command. If Hermes is present, offer to run it. If Hermes is missing, print official install steps. Do not fake a pass.
7. Write the routine folder only after that pass, or after the teammate accepts the printed command. Save copies the skills into the routine. Then offer `dora review --quick` on each copy. The teammate can skip.
8. After `dora harness boot`, tell the teammate to run `hermes mcp login scalekit`. Dora does not run that login. If a refresh token dies, run that command again. If the Scalekit connected account is dead, open the provider link again.

Do not ask for the loop interval during this grill. Default is 1 hour. Ask after a good run.

```bash
dora harness new --accept --yes --slug <slug> --prompt-file <prompt.md> --mcp-url <url> --skills-run <name|path|url> --skills-refer <name|path|url>
70→```

MUST collect the gate before save.
MUST accept none for skills to run and skills to refer.
MUST copy named skills into the routine.
MUST NOT require a skill because a connector exists.
MUST NOT write the original skill directory.
MUST NOT invent a registry, a slug, a connector, or a loop interval.
MUST NOT write the folder when the idea is not loop-able.

1→---
name: writing-for-agents
description: Writing documents for agents. Use when creating or editing skills, or modifying AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.
---

Reference for writing any document an agent consumes — a skill, an `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`, a doc reached by a pointer. The packaging differs; the writing does not: the same levers make each one predictable — the agent taking the same _process_ every run, not producing the same output.

When the document you're writing is a skill, read [`SKILL-MECHANICS.md`](SKILL-MECHANICS.md) for frontmatter, invocation choice, and router skills.

10→## Context pointers

A **context pointer** is a reference held in the agent's context that names some out-of-context material and encodes the condition for reaching it. A skill's description is one; a line in `AGENTS.md` naming a doc is the same object. The pointer's _wording_, not its target, decides when the agent reaches the material — and how reliably. A must-have target behind a weakly worded pointer is a variance bug: sharpen the wording first, and inline the material only if sharpening fails.

A pointer does two jobs — state what the material is, and list the **branches** that should trigger reaching it (a branch is a distinct case the document handles, so different runs take different paths through it). Every word of an always-loaded pointer costs on every turn, so it earns even harder pruning than the body:

- **Front-load the leading word** — the pointer is where it does its triggering work.
- **One trigger per branch.** Synonyms that rename a single branch are one branch written twice; collapse them and keep only genuinely distinct branches.
- **Cut identity the body already carries.**

20→## The two loads

Every document and pointer you add spends one of two budgets:

- **Context load** — the cost of always-loaded material on the agent's window: an `AGENTS.md` line, a skill description, anything sitting in context every turn, spending tokens and attention whether or not it fires.
- **Cognitive load** — the cost on the human: which documents exist and when to reach for each. The human is the index. Not a cost to minimise — it is the price of human agency; spend it where human judgement matters, remove it where it does not.

Material reached only through a pointer escapes context load at the price of the pointer's own line; material with no pointer at all rides entirely on cognitive load.

## Information hierarchy
30→
A document is built from two content types — **steps** (the ordered actions the agent performs) and **reference** (definitions, rules, facts consulted on demand) — that mix freely: all steps (a recipe), all reference (a review's rules, this skill), or both. 2. **In-file reference** — consulted on demand. Often a legitimately flat peer-set (every rule of a review on one rung) — a fine arrangement, not a smell.
3. **Disclosed reference** — pushed out into a separate file, reached by a context pointer, loaded only when the pointer fires. Spans a sibling file in the same folder through fully external reference that lives anywhere and any document can point at.

Not primarily a token optimisation: it is how the hierarchy is protected. Keep a concept's definition, rules, and caveats under one heading rather than scattered, so reading one part brings its neighbours with it. The test: the document should read like documentation written for the agent — grouped material reads that way; scattered material does not. Every step ends on a **completion criterion** — the condition that tells the agent the work is done. Two properties make it a lever:

- **Clarity** — can the agent tell done from not-done? 1→---
name: review-with-dora
description: >-
  Use when reviewing agent context (SKILL.md, plugin, rule, AGENTS.md) with
  dora before reporting done. Also when ask-dora routes a Dora job (review,
  fix, unused, scan), or the user asks to review, diagnose, or clean up
  Claude, Cursor, Codex, Copilot, or Grok context.
---

10→# review-with-dora

You run `dora`. **Review** is the gate. Done means **exit 0**.

If `dora` is not on `PATH`, use `npx @hacksmith/doraval`.

## The loop

1. **Review.** `dora review --quick` on a new repo. After an edit, `dora review --quick <path>`.
   `<path>` is the Skill directory, a plugin root, or `.`.
20→   More than 10 artifacts: pass a path or `--all`.
   Done: Findings read, exit code read. **exit 0** is the only report-done.

2. **Author** only when the user asked you to write a Skill, Rule, agent, or plugin.
   `dora skill new` / `dora rule new` / `dora agent new` / `dora plugin new`.
   Done: the files exist.

3. **Mechanical fix.**
   ```bash
   dora fix <path> --dry-run
30→   dora fix <path> --yes
   ```
   `--yes` applies frontmatter, formatting, and missing fields.
   Done: dry-run is clean, or `--yes` applied.

4. **Judgment.** Run Brief. Then **replace**.
   `dora fix <path> --brief` (or `--json`).
   Each item: `message`, `severity`, `hint`, optional `code` / `docUrl`.
   Target is that Authored `SKILL.md`.

40→   **Replace** one item at a time:
   - Name the intended rule in one sentence. Write the smallest wording that states it.
   - Put that wording where the old sentence lived. One home.
   - Stay inside the span the item names.
   - Imperative. One statement of the rule.
   - Skill already states the rule → show the Finding, leave the file.
   - Stay in this Skill's files. A size Finding may move text into this Skill's `references/`.

   Done: every item replaced or shown. Then step 5.

50→5. **Re-review.** `dora review --quick <path>` after every edit.
   Done: **exit 0**. That is the only report-done.

6. **Delegated Judge** only after step 5 is **exit 0** and a later Review (no `--quick`) is `delegated`.
   Read `JUDGE THIS`. Evaluate. Fix Findings.
   Done: mechanical tiers clean and the rubric applied.
   Branch on JSON: [output.md](references/output.md).

Add `--format json` when you will branch on fields. Add `--ci` in CI.

60→## Writes

Pass `--yes` or `--dry-run` on `fix`, `conflicts`, `memory promote`, `skill remove`, `skill restore`, `probe`, `harness new --accept`, and `config set` of a secret.
`--brief` is not a write. A missing write flag is **exit 2**.

## Side paths

Verbs: [commands.md](references/commands.md). Exit codes and JSON: [output.md](references/output.md).
Flags: `dora <command> --help`. Map: `dora --help --json`.
